_readme: HOW IMPORTED STOCK SELLS DOWN — the price ladder and the demand patterns.
EVERY FIGURE HERE IS MIKE'S, read out of design/report-source-models/Import &
Retail.xlsx on 2026-09-04. The ladder is `Supplier 1 Inputs` row 19 (New Stock /
Std Retail / Runout markups, with their stock-turn day bands beside them); the
patterns are the four-band sell-through table the supplier sheets consume. Nothing
here was chosen by a developer, and nothing should be.
WHY IT IS A FILE AND NOT A CONSTANT: it is advisory content that moves the numbers
on a client's forecast, so somebody must be able to see it and change it. It is
MENTOR-TIER content — the stated judgement of the drawing, following the default of
2026-08-24 — and cascades to a firm the first time one has a real reason to price
differently.
A pattern's four bands are 30 days each and MUST total 1. The ladder's markups are
on COST, so a price is cost x (1 + markup): 145 x 2.85 = 413.25, which is the
workbook's own New Stock Retail Price for Stock 1.
TERMS — the supplier's, and they are what turn an ORDER DATE into a landing date.
Manufacture 120, balance due 91 days from order, 9 pre-retail prep days, interest
cover 6%, and the three shipping speeds: all Mike's, same workbook. They summed to
the 154 / 149 / 144 day totals his sheet states for sea, air and express.
THEY MOVE MONEY, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE HERE. Interest cover is charged on the
deferred balance and expensed in overheads; the day counts decide which calendar
month every deposit, balance and landing falls in. Until 2026-09-04 all seven were
hardcoded in components/ThreeWayForecastIntake.vue with a badge on screen claiming
they came from platform settings, which was untrue — nothing could edit them. Mike's
instruction that day: 'make it editable'.
UNITS ARE THE ENGINE'S, as with the markups: interestCoverPct is a DECIMAL (0.06 =
6%). The screen shows a percentage and converts on both edges.
